, out of which We produce grain, heaped up
; out of the date-palm and its sheaths
clus ters of dates hanging low and near: and
gardens of grapes, and olives, and pomegranates, each similar
: when they begin to bear fruit, feast your eyes with the fruit and the ripeness thereof. Behold! in these things there are signs for people who believe

6:100.t: Yet they make the Jinns equals with God, though God did create the Jinns; and they falsely, having no knowledge, attribute to Him sons and daughters. Praise and glory be to Him!
above what they attribute to Him

6:101.t: To Him is due the primal origin of the heavens and the earth: How can He have a son when He hath no consort? He created all things, and He hath full knowledge of all things

6:102.t: That is God, your Lord! there is no god but He, the Creator of all things: then worship ye Him: and He hath power to dispose of all affairs

6:103.t: No vision can grasp Him, but His grasp is over all vision: He is above all comprehension, yet is acquainted with all things

6:104.t: Now have come to you, from your Lord, proofs
: if any will see, it will be for
his own soul; if any will be blind, it will be to his own

6:105.t: Thus do we explain the signs by various
: that they may say, "Thou hast taught
diligently," and that We may make the matter clear to those who know

6:106.t: Follow what thou art taught by inspiration from thy Lord: there is no god but He: and turn aside from those who join gods with God

6:107.t: If it had been God's plan, they would not have taken false gods: but We made thee not one to watch over their doings, nor art thou set over them to dispose of their affairs

6:108.t: Revile not ye those whom they call upon besides God, lest they out of spite revile God in their ignorance. Thus have We made alluring to each people its own doings. In the end will they return to their Lord, and We shall then tell them the trut h of all that they did

6:109.t: They swear their strongest oaths by God, that if a
sign came to them, by it they would believe. Say: "Certainly
signs are in the power of God: but what will make you
signs came, they wi ll not believe

6:110.t: their hearts and their eyes, even as they refused to believe in this in the first instance: We shall leave them in their trespasses, to wander in distraction

6:111.t: Even if We did send unto them angels, and the dead did speak unto them, and We gathered together all things before their very eyes, they are not the ones to believe, unless it is in God's plan. But most of them ignore

6:112.t: Likewise did We make for every Messenger an enemy,- evil ones among men and jinns, inspiring each other with flowery discourses by way of deception. If thy Lord had so planned, they would not have done it: so leave them and their inventions al one

6:113.t: let the hearts of those incline, who have no faith in the hereafter: let them delight in it, and let them earn from it what they may

6:114.t: Say: "Shall I seek for judge other than God? - when He it is Who hath sent unto you the Book, explained in detail." They know full well, to whom We have given the Book, that it hath been sent down from thy Lord in truth. Never be then of those who doubt

6:115.t: The word of thy Lord doth find its fulfilment in truth and in justice: None can change His words: for He is the one who heareth and knoweth all

6:116.t: Wert thou to follow the common run of those on earth, they will lead thee away from the way of God. They follow nothing but conjecture: they do nothing but lie

6:117.t: Thy Lord knoweth best who strayeth from His way: He knoweth best who they are that receive His guidance

6:118.t: on which God's name hath been pronounced, if ye have faith in His signs

6:119.t: Why should ye not eat of
on which God's name hath been pronounced, when He hath explained to you in detail what is forbidden to you - except under compulsion of necessity? But many do mislead
by their appetites unchecked by knowl edge. Thy Lord knoweth best those who transgress

6:120.t: Eschew all sin, open or secret: those who earn sin will get due recompense for their "earnings

6:121.t: on which God's name hath not been pronounced: That would be impiety. But the evil ones ever inspire their friends to contend with you if ye were to obey them, ye would indeed be Pagans

6:122.t: Can he who was dead, to whom We gave life, and a light whereby he can walk amongst men, be like him who is in the depths of darkness, from which he can never come out? Thus to those without faith their own deeds seem pleasing

6:123.t: Thus have We placed leaders in every town, its wicked men, to plot
therein: but they only plot against their own souls, and they perceive it not

6:124.t: When there comes to them a sign
, They say: "We shall not believe until we receive one
like those received by God's apostles." God knoweth best where
to carry out His mission. Soon will the wicked be overtaken by humiliation before God, and a severe punishment, for all their plots

6:125.t: willeth to guide,- He openeth their breast to Islam; those whom He willeth to leave straying,- He maketh their breast close and constricted, as if they had to climb up to the skies: thus doth God
the penalty on those who refuse to believe

6:126.t: This is the way of thy Lord, leading straight: We have detailed the signs for those who receive admonition

6:127.t: For them will be a home of peace in the presence of their Lord: He will be their friend, because they practised

6:128.t: One day will He gather them all together,
did ye take of men." Their friends amongst men will say: "Our Lord! we made profit from each other: but

we reached our term - which thou didst ap point for us." He will say: "The Fire be your dwelling-place: you will dwell therein for ever, except as God willeth." for thy Lord is full of wisdom and knowledge

6:129.t: Thus do we make the wrong-doers turn to each other, because of what they earn

6:130.t: O ye assembly of Jinns and men! came there not unto you apostles from amongst you, setting forth unto you My signs, and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say: "We bear witness against ourselves." It was the life of t his world that deceived them. So against themselves will they bear witness that they rejected Faith

6:131.t: thus, for thy Lord would not destroy for their wrong-doing men's habitations whilst their occupants were unwarned

6:132.t: according to their deeds: for thy Lord is not unmindful of anything that they do

6:133.t: Thy Lord is self-sufficient, full of Mercy: if it were His will, He could destroy you, and in your place appoint whom He will as your successors, even as He raised you up from the posterity of other people

6:134.t: All that hath been promised unto you will come to pass: nor can ye frustrate it

6:135.t: Say: "O my people! Do whatever ye can: I will do
: soon will ye know who it is whose end will be
in the Hereafter: certain it is that the wrong- doers will not prosper

6:136.t: Out of what God hath produced in abundance in tilth and in cattle, they assigned Him a share: they say, according to their fancies: "This is for God, and this" - for our "partners"! but the share of their" partners "reacheth not God, whilst the share of God reacheth their "partners"! evil

6:137.t: Even so, in the eyes of most of the pagans, their "partners" made alluring the slaughter of their children, in order to lead them to their own destruction, and cause confusion in their religion. If God had willed, they would not have done so: B ut leave alone them and their inventions

6:138.t: And they say that such and such cattle and crops are taboo, and none should eat of them except those whom - so they say - We wish; further, there are cattle forbidden to yoke or burden, and cattle on which,
, the name of God is n ot pronounced; - inventions against God's name: soon will He requite them for their inventions

6:139.t: They say: "What is in the wombs of such and such cattle is specially reserved
for our men, and forbidden to our women; but if it is still-born, then all have share therein. For their
, He will soon punish them: for He is full of wisdom and knowledge

6:140.t: Lost are those who slay their children, from folly, without knowledge, and forbid food which God hath provided for them, inventing
against God. They have indeed gone astray and heeded no guidance

6:141.t: It is He Who produceth gardens, with trellises and without, and dates, and tilth with produce of all kinds, and olives and pomegranates, similar
: eat of their fruit in their season, but render the dues that are proper on the day that the harvest is gathered. But waste not by excess: for God loveth not the wasters

6:142.t: Of the cattle are some for burden and some for meat: eat what God hath provided for you, and follow not the footsteps of Satan: for he is to you and avowed enemy

6:143.t: pairs: of sheep a pair, and of goats a pair; say, hath He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or
which the wombs of the two females enclose? Tell me with knowledge if ye are truthful

6:144.t: Of camels a pair, and oxen a pair; say, hath He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or

which the wombs of the two females enclose? - Were ye present when God ordered you such a thing? But who doth more wrong than one who invents a lie against God, to lead astray men without knowledge? For God guideth not people who do wrong

6:145.t: Say: "I find not in the message received by me by inspiration any
forbidden to be eaten by one who wishes to eat it, unless it be dead meat, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine,- for it is an abomination - or, what is impious,
on which a name has been invoked, other than God's". But
, if a person is forced by necessity, without wilful disobedience, nor transgressing due limits,- thy Lord is Oft-forgiving, Most Merciful

6:146.t: For those who followed the Jewish Law, We forbade every

with undivided hoof, and We forbade them that fat of the ox and the sheep, except what adheres to their backs or their entrails, or is mixed up with a bone: this in recompense fo r their wilful disobedience: for We are true

6:147.t: If they accuse thee of falsehood, say: "Your Lord is full of mercy all- embracing; but from people in guilt never will His wrath be turned back

6:148.t: will say: "If God had wished, we should not have given partners to Him nor would our fathers; nor should we have had any taboos." So did their ancestors argue falsely, until they tasted of Our wrath. Say: "Have ye any
knowledge? If so, produce it before us. Ye follow nothing but conjecture: ye do nothing but lie

6:149.t: Say: "With God is the argument that reaches home: if it had been His will, He could indeed have guided you all

6:150.t: Say: "Bring forward your witnesses to prove that God did forbid so and so." If they bring such witnesses, be not thou amongst them: Nor follow thou the vain desires of such as treat our signs as falsehoods, and such as believe not in the Herea fter: for they hold others as equal with their Guardian-Lord

6:151.t: Say: "Come, I will rehearse what God hath

prohibited you from": Join not anything as equal with Him; be good to your parents; kill not your children on a plea of want;- We provide sustenance for you and for them;- come not nigh to sha meful deeds. Whether open or secret; take not life, which God hath made sacred, except by way of justice and law: thus doth He command you, that ye may learn wisdom

6:152.t: And come not nigh to the orphan's property, except to improve it, until he attain the age of full strength; give measure and weight with

justice;- no burden do We place on any soul, but that which it can bear;- whenever ye speak, speak j ustly, even if a near relative is concerned; and fulfil the covenant of God: thus doth He command you, that ye may remember

6:153.t: Verily, this is My way, leading straight: follow it: follow not
paths: they will scatter you about from His
path: thus doth He command you. that ye may be righteous

6:154.t: Moreover, We gave Moses the Book, completing
to those who would do right, and explaining all things in detail,- and a guide and a mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord

6:155.t: And this is a Book which We have revealed as a blessing: so follow it and be righteous, that ye may receive mercy

6:156.t: Lest ye should say: "The Book was sent down to two Peoples before us, and for our part, we remained unacquainted with all that they learned by assiduous study

6:157.t: Or lest ye should say: "If the Book had only been sent down to us, we should have followed its guidance better than they." Now then hath come unto you a clear

from your Lord,- and a guide and a mercy: then who could do more wrong than o ne who rejecteth God's signs, and turneth away therefrom? In good time shall We requite those who turn away from Our signs, with a dreadful penalty, for their turning away

6:158.t: Are they waiting to see if the angels come to them, or thy Lord

, or certain of the signs of thy Lord! the day that certain of the signs of thy Lord do come, no good will it do to a soul to believe in them then if it believed not befor e nor earned righteousness through its faith. Say: "Wait ye: we too are waiting

6:159.t: As for those who divide their religion and break up into sects, thou hast no part in them in the least: their affair is with God: He will in the end tell them the truth of all that they did

6:160.t: He that doeth good shall have ten times as much to his credit: He that doeth evil shall only be recompensed according to his evil: no wrong shall be done unto

6:161.t: Say: "Verily, my Lord hath guided me to a way that is straight,- a religion of right,- the path
by Abraham the true in Faith, and he

6:162.t: Say: "Truly, my prayer and my service of sacrifice, my life and my death, are
for God, the Cherisher of the Worlds

6:163.t: No partner hath He: this am I commanded, and I am the first of those who bow to His will

6:164.t: Cherisher other than God, when He is the Cherisher of all things

? Every soul draws the meed of its acts on none but itself: no bearer of burdens can bear of burdens can bear the burden of another. Your goal in the end is towards God: He will tell you the truth of the things wherein ye disputed

6:165.t: It is He Who hath made you

agents, inheritors of the earth: He hath raised you in ranks, some above others: that He may try you in the gifts He hath given you: for thy Lord is quick in punishment: yet He is indeed Oft-forgiving, Most Mer ciful

7:2.t: A Book revealed unto thee,- So let thy heart be oppressed no more by any difficulty on that account,- that with it thou mightest warn

7:3.t: the revelation given unto you from your Lord, and follow not, as friends or protectors, other than Him. Little it is ye remember of admonition

7:4.t: How many towns have We destroyed
? Our punishment took them on a sudden by night or while they slept for their afternoon rest

7:5.t: Our punishment took them, no cry did they utter but this: "Indeed we did wrong

7:6.t: Then shall we question those to whom Our message was sent and those by whom We sent it

7:7.t: And verily, We shall recount their whole story with knowledge, for We were never absent

7:8.t: The balance that day will be true

7:9.t: Those whose scale will be light, will be their souls in perdition, for that they wrongfully treated Our signs

7:10.t: It is We Who have placed you with authority on earth, and provided you therein with means for the fulfilment of your life: small are the thanks that ye give

7:11.t: It is We Who created you and gave you shape; then We bade the angels bow down to Adam, and they bowed down; not so Iblis; He refused to be of those who bow down

7:12.t: said: "What prevented thee from bowing down when I commanded thee?" He said: "I am better than he: Thou didst create me from fire, and him from clay

7:13.t: said: "Get thee down from this: it is not for thee to be arrogant here: get out, for thou art of the meanest

7:14.t: He said: "Give me respite till the day they are raised up

7:15.t: said: "Be thou among those who have respite

7:16.t: He said: "Because thou hast thrown me out of the way, lo! I will lie in wait for them on thy straight way

7:17.t: Then will I assault them from before them and behind them, from their right and their left: Nor wilt thou find, in most of them, gratitude

7:18.t: said: "Get out from this, disgraced and expelled. If any of them follow thee,- Hell will I fill with you all

7:19.t: O Adam! dwell thou and thy wife in the Garden, and enjoy
as ye wish: but approach not this tree, or ye run into harm and transgression

7:20.t: Then began Satan to whisper suggestions to them, bringing openly before their minds all their shame that was hidden from them
: he said: "Your Lord only forbade you this tree, lest ye should become angels or such beings as live for eve r

7:21.t: And he swore to them both, that he was their sincere adviser

7:22.t: So by deceit he brought about their fall: when they tasted of the tree, their shame became manifest to them, and they began to sew together the leaves of the garden over their bodies. And their Lord called unto them: "Did I not forbid you that tree, and tell you that Satan was an avowed enemy unto you

7:23.t: They said: "Our Lord! We have wronged our own souls: If thou forgive us not and bestow not upon us Thy Mercy, we shall certainly be lost

7:24.t: said: "Get ye down. With enmity between yourselves. On earth will be your dwelling-place and your means of livelihood,- for a time

7:25.t: He said: "Therein shall ye live, and therein shall ye die; but from it shall ye be taken out

7:26.t: O ye Children of Adam! We have bestowed raiment upon you to cover your shame, as well as to be an adornment to you. But the raiment of righteousness,- that is the best. Such are among the Signs of God, that they may receive admonition

7:27.t: O ye Children of Adam! Let not Satan seduce you, in the same manner as He got your parents out of the Garden, stripping them of their raiment, to expose their shame: for he and his tribe watch you from a position where ye cannot see them: We m ade the evil ones friends

7:28.t: When they do aught that is shameful, they say: "We found our fathers doing so"; and "God commanded us thus": Say: "Nay, God never commands what is shameful: do ye say of God what ye know not

7:29.t: Say: "My Lord hath commanded justice; and that ye set your whole selves
at every time and place of prayer, and call upon Him, making your devotion sincere as in His sight: such as He created you in the beginning, so shall ye return

7:30.t: Some He hath guided: Others have
deserved the loss of their way; in that they took the evil ones, in preference to God, for their friends and protectors, and think that they receive guidance

7:31.t: O Children of Adam! wear your beautiful apparel at every time and place of prayer: eat and drink: But waste not by excess, for God loveth not the wasters

7:32.t: Say: Who hath forbidden the beautiful
of God, which He hath produced for His servants, and the things, clean and pure,
for sustenance? Say: They are, in the life of this world, for those who believe,
pure ly for them on the Day of Judgment. Thus do We explain the signs in detail for those who understand

7:33.t: Say: the things that my Lord hath indeed forbidden are: shameful deeds, whether open or secret; sins and trespasses against truth or reason; assigning of partners to God, for which He hath given no authority; and saying things about God of whi ch ye have no knowledge

7:34.t: To every people is a term appointed: when their term is reached, not an hour can they cause delay, nor

7:35.t: O ye Children of Adam! whenever there come to you apostles from amongst you, rehearsing My signs unto you,- those who are righteous and mend
,- on them shall be no fear nor shall they grieve

7:36.t: But those who reject Our signs and treat them with arrogance,- they are companions of the Fire, to dwell therein

7:37.t: Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against God or rejects His Signs? For such, their portion appointed must reach them from the Book

arrive and take their souls, they say: "Where a re the things that ye used to invoke besides God?" They will reply, "They have left us in the lurch," And they will bear witness against themselves, that they had rejected God

7:38.t: He will say: "Enter ye in the company of the peoples who passed away before you - men and jinns, - into the Fire." Every time a new people enters, it curses its sister-people

, until they follow each other, all into the Fire. Saith the last about the first: "Our Lord! it is these that misled us: so give them a double penalty in the Fire." He will say: "Doubled for all": but this ye do not understand

7:39.t: Then the first will say to the last: "See then! No advantage have ye over us; so taste ye of the penalty for all that ye did

7:40.t: To those who reject Our signs and treat them with arrogance, no opening will there be of the gates of heaven, nor will they enter the garden, until the camel can pass through the eye of the needle: Such is Our reward for those in sin

7:41.t: For them there is Hell, as a couch
and folds and folds of covering above: such is Our requital of those who do wrong

7:42.t: But those who believe and work righteousness,- no burden do We place on any soul, but that which it can bear,- they will be Companions of the Garden, therein to dwell

7:43.t: And We shall remove from their hearts any lurking sense of injury;- beneath them will be rivers flowing;- and they shall say: "Praise be to God, who hath guided us to this

: never could we have found guidance, had it not been for the guidance of God: indeed it was the truth, that the apostles of our Lord brought unto us." And they shall hear the cry: "Behold! the garden before you! Ye have been made its inheritors, for your deeds

7:44.t: The Companions of the Garden will call out to the Companions of the Fire: "We have indeed found the promises of our Lord to us true: Have you also found Your Lord's promises true?" They shall say, "Yes"; but a crier shall proclaim between them: "The curse of God is on the wrong-doers

7:45.t: from the path of God and would seek in it something crooked: they were those who denied the Hereafter

7:46.t: Between them shall be a veil, and on the heights will be men who would know every one by his marks: they will call out to the Companions of the Garden, "peace on you": they will not have entered, but they will have an assurance

7:47.t: When their eyes shall be turned towards the Companions of the Fire, they will say: "Our Lord! send us not to the company of the wrong-doers

7:48.t: The men on the heights will call to certain men whom they will know from their marks, saying: "Of what profit to you were your hoards and your arrogant ways

7:49.t: Behold! are these not the men whom you swore that God with His Mercy would never bless? Enter ye the Garden: no fear shall be on you, nor shall ye grieve

7:50.t: The Companions of the Fire will call to the Companions of the Garden: "Pour down to us water or anything that God doth provide for your sustenance." They will say: "Both these things hath God forbidden to those who rejected Him

7:51.t: Such as took their religion to be mere amusement and play, and were deceived by the life of the world." That day shall We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs, and as they were wont to reject Our signs

7:52.t: For We had certainly sent unto them a Book, based on knowledge, which We explained in detail,- a guide and a mercy to all who believe

7:53.t: Do they just wait for the final fulfilment of the event? On the day the event is finally fulfilled, those who disregarded it before will say: "The apostles of our Lord did indeed bring true

. Have we no intercessors now to intercede on our behalf? Or could we be sent back? then should we behave differently from our behaviour in the past." In fact they will have lost their souls, and the things they invented will leave them in the lurch

7:54.t: Your Guardian-Lord is God, Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and is firmly established on the throne
: He draweth the night as a veil o'er the day, each seeking the other in rapid succession: He created the sun, t he moon, and the stars,
governed by laws under His command. Is it not His to create and to govern? Blessed be God, the Cherisher and Sustainer of the worlds

7:55.t: Call on your Lord with humility and in private: for God loveth not those who trespass beyond bounds

7:56.t: Do no mischief on the earth, after it hath been set in order, but call on Him with fear and longing
: for the Mercy of God is
near to those who do good

7:57.t: It is He Who sendeth the winds like heralds of glad tidings, going before His mercy: when they have carried the heavy-laden clouds, We drive them to a land that is dead, make rain to descend thereon, and produce every kind of harvest therewith: thus shall We raise up the dead: perchance ye may remember

7:58.t: From the land that is clean and good, by the will of its Cherisher, springs up produce,
after its kind: but from the land that is bad, springs up nothing but that which is niggardly: thus do we explain the signs by various
to t hose who are grateful

7:59.t: We sent Noah to his people. He said: "O my people! worship God! ye have no other god but Him. I fear for you the punishment of a dreadful day

7:60.t: The leaders of his people said: "Ah! we see thee evidently wandering

7:61.t: He said: "O my people! No wandering is there in my
: on the contrary I am an apostle from the Lord and Cherisher of the worlds

7:62.t: I but fulfil towards you the duties of my Lord's mission: Sincere is my advice to you, and I know from God something that ye know not

7:63.t: Do ye wonder that there hath come to you a message from your Lord, through a man of your own people, to warn you,- so that ye may fear God and haply receive His Mercy

7:64.t: But they rejected him, and We delivered him, and those with him, in the Ark: but We overwhelmed in the flood those who rejected Our signs. They were indeed a blind people

7:65.t: brethren: He said: O my people! worship God! ye have no other god but Him will ye not fear

7:66.t: The leaders of the Unbelievers among his people said: "Ah! we see thou art an imbecile!" and "We think thou art a liar

7:67.t: He said: "O my people! I am no imbecile, but
an apostle from the Lord and Cherisher of the worlds

7:68.t: I but fulfil towards you the duties of my Lord's mission: I am to you a sincere and trustworthy adviser

7:69.t: Do ye wonder that there hath come to you a message from your Lord through a man of your own people, to warn you? call in remembrance that He made you inheritors after the people of Noah, and gave you a stature tall among the nations. Call in remembrance the benefits
from God: that so ye may prosper

7:70.t: They said: "Comest thou to us, that we may worship God alone, and give up the cult of our fathers? bring us what thou threatenest us with, if so be that thou tellest the truth

7:71.t: He said: "Punishment and wrath have already come upon you from your Lord: dispute ye with me over names which ye have devised - ye and your fathers,- without authority from God? then wait: I am amongst you, also waiting

7:72.t: We saved him and those who adhered to him. By Our mercy, and We cut off the roots of those who rejected Our signs and did not believe

7:73.t: Salih, one of their own brethren: He said: "O my people! worship God: ye have no other god but Him. Now hath come unto you a clear
from your Lord! This she-camel of God is a Sign unto you: So leave her to graze in God's earth, and let her come to no harm, or ye shall be seized with a grievous punishment

7:74.t: And remember how He made you inheritors after the 'Ad people and gave you habitations in the land: ye build for yourselves palaces and castles in
plains, and care out homes in the mountains; so bring to remembrance the benefits
from God, and refrain from evil and mischief on the earth

7:75.t: The leaders of the arrogant party among his people said to those who were reckoned powerless - those among them who believed: "know ye indeed that Salih is an apostle from his Lord?" They said: "We do indeed believe in the revelation which hat h been sent through him

7:76.t: The Arrogant party said: "For our part, we reject what ye believe in

7:77.t: Then they ham-strung the she-camel, and insolently defied the order of their Lord, saying: "O Salih! bring about thy threats, if thou art an apostle

7:78.t: So the earthquake took them unawares, and they lay prostrate in their homes in the morning

7:79.t: So Salih left them, saying: "O my people! I did indeed convey to you the message for which I was sent by my Lord: I gave you good counsel, but ye love not good counsellors

7:80.t: Lut: He said to his people: "Do ye commit lewdness such as no people in creation

7:81.t: For ye practise your lusts on men in preference to women: ye are indeed a people transgressing beyond bounds

7:82.t: And his people gave no answer but this: they said, "Drive them out of your city: these are indeed men who want to be clean and pure

7:83.t: But we saved him and his family, except his wife: she was of those who legged behind

7:84.t: And we rained down on them a shower
: Then see what was the end of those who indulged in sin and crime

7:85.t: To the Madyan people We sent Shu'aib, one of their own brethren: he said: "O my people! worship God; Ye have no other god but Him. Now hath come unto you a clear

from your Lord! Give just measure and weight, nor withhold from the people the things that are their due; and do no mischief on the earth after it has been set in order: that will be best for you, if ye have Faith

7:86.t: And squat not on every road, breathing threats, hindering from the path of God those who believe in Him, and seeking in it something crooked; But remember how ye were little, and He gave you increase. And hold in your mind's eye what was the end of those who did mischief

7:87.t: And if there is a party among you who believes in the message with which I have been sent, and a party which does not believe, hold yourselves in patience until God doth decide between us: for He is the best to decide

7:88.t: The leaders, the arrogant party among his people, said: "O Shu'aib! we shall certainly drive thee out of our city -
and those who believe with thee; or else ye
shall have to return to our ways and religion." He said: "Wha t! even though we do detest

7:89.t: We should indeed invent a lie against God, if we returned to your ways after God hath rescued us therefrom; nor could we by any manner of means return thereto unless it be as in the will and plan of God, Our Lord. Our Lord can reach out to th e utmost recesses of things by His knowledge. In the God is our trust. our Lord! decide Thou between us and our people in truth, for Thou art the best to decide

7:90.t: The leaders, the unbelievers among his people, said: "If ye follow Shu'aib, be sure then ye are ruined

7:91.t: But the earthquake took them unawares, and they lay prostrate in their homes before the morning

7:92.t: The men who reject Shu'aib became as if they had never been in the homes where they had flourished: the men who rejected Shu'aib - it was they who were ruined

7:93.t: So Shu'aib left them, saying: "O my people! I did indeed convey to you the messages for which I was sent by my Lord: I gave you good counsel, but how shall I lament over a people who refuse to believe

7:94.t: Whenever We sent a prophet to a town, We took up its people in suffering and adversity, in order that they might learn humility

7:95.t: Then We changed their suffering into prosperity, until they grew and multiplied, and began to say: "Our fathers
were touched by suffering and affluence"... Behold! We called them to account of a sudden, while they realised not

7:96.t: If the people of the towns had but believed and feared God, We should indeed have opened out to them
blessings from heaven and earth; but they rejected
, and We brought them to book for their misdeeds

7:97.t: Did the people of the towns feel secure against the coming of Our wrath by night while they were asleep

7:98.t: Or else did they feel secure against its coming in broad daylight while they played about

7:99.t: Did they then feel secure against the plan of God?- but no one can feel secure from the Plan of God, except those

7:100.t: To those who inherit the earth in succession to its
possessors, is it not a guiding,
that, if We so willed, We could punish them
for their sins, and seal up their hearts so that they could not hear

7:101.t: Such were the towns whose story We
relate unto thee: There came indeed to them their apostles with clear
: But they would not believe what they had rejected before. Thus doth God seal up the hearts of those who reject faith

7:102.t: Most of them We found not men
to their covenant: but most of them We found rebellious and disobedient

7:103.t: Then after them We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wrongfully rejected them: So see what was the end of those who made mischief

7:104.t: Moses said: "O Pharaoh! I am an apostle from the Lord of the worlds

7:105.t: One for whom it is right to say nothing but truth about God. Now have I come unto you
, from your Lord, with a clear
: So let the Children of Israel depart along with me

7:106.t: said: "If indeed thou hast come with a Sign, show it forth,- if thou tellest the truth

7:107.t: threw his rod, and behold! it was a serpent, plain

7:108.t: And he drew out his hand, and behold! it was white to all beholders

7:109.t: Said the Chiefs of the people of Pharaoh: "This is indeed a sorcerer well- versed

7:110.t: His plan is to get you out of your land: then what is it ye counsel

7:111.t: They said: "Keep him and his brother in suspense
; and send to the cities men to collect

7:112.t: And bring up to thee all

7:113.t: So there came the sorcerers to Pharaoh: They said, "of course we shall have a

7:114.t: ,- for ye shall in that case be

7:115.t: They said: "O Moses! wilt thou throw

7:116.t: ." So when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people, and struck terror into them: for they showed a great

7:117.t: We put it into Moses's mind by inspiration: "Throw
thy rod":and behold! it swallows up straight away all the falsehoods which they fake

7:118.t: Thus truth was confirmed, and all that they did was made of no effect

7:119.t: were vanquished there and then, and were made to look small

7:120.t: But the sorcerers fell down prostrate in adoration

7:121.t: Saying: "We believe in the Lord of the Worlds

7:122.t: The Lord of Moses and Aaron

7:123.t: Said Pharaoh: "Believe ye in Him before I give you permission? Surely this is a trick which ye have planned in the city to drive out its people: but soon shall ye know

7:124.t: Be sure I will cut off your hands and your feet on apposite sides, and I will cause you all to die on the cross

7:125.t: They said: "For us, We are but sent back unto our Lord

7:126.t: But thou dost wreak thy vengeance on us simply because we believed in the Signs of our Lord when they reached us! Our Lord! pour out on us patience and constancy, and take our souls unto thee as Muslims

7:127.t: Said the chiefs of Pharaoh's people: "Wilt thou leave Moses and his people, to spread mischief in the land, and to abandon thee and thy gods?" He said: "Their male children will we slay;
their females will we save alive; and we have over them

7:128.t: Said Moses to his people: "Pray for help from God, and
in patience and constancy: for the earth is God's, to give as a heritage to such of His servants as He pleaseth; and the end is

7:129.t: trouble, both before and after thou camest to us." He said: "It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you inheritors in the earth; that so He may try you by your deeds

7:130.t: We punished the people of Pharaoh with years
and shortness of crops; that they might receive admonition

7:131.t: came, they said, "This is due to us;" When gripped by calamity, they ascribed it to evil omens connected with Moses and those with him! Behold! in truth the omens of evil are theirs in God's sight, but most of them do not understand

7:132.t: : "Whatever be the Signs thou bringest, to work therewith thy sorcery on us, we shall never believe in thee

7:133.t: on them: Wholesale death, Locusts, Lice, Frogs, And Blood: Signs openly self-explained: but they were steeped in arrogance,- a people given to sin

7:134.t: Every time the penalty fell on them, they said: "O Moses! on your behalf call on thy Lord in virtue of his promise to thee: If thou wilt remove the penalty from us, we shall truly believe in thee, and we shall send away the Children of Israel w ith thee

7:135.t: But every time We removed the penalty from them according to a fixed term which they had to fulfil,- Behold! they broke their word

7:136.t: So We exacted retribution from them: We drowned them in the sea, because they rejected Our Signs and failed to take warning from them

7:137.t: And We made a people, considered weak

, inheritors of lands in both east and west, - lands whereon We sent down Our blessings. The fair promise of thy Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel, because they had patience and constancy, and We levelled to the ground the great works and fine buildings which Pharaoh and his people erected

7:138.t: We took the Children of Israel

across the sea. They came upon a people devoted entirely to some idols they had. They said: "O Moses! fashion for us a god like unto the gods they have." He said: "Surely ye are a people without kn owledge

7:139.t: As to these folk,- the cult they are in is
a fragment of a ruin, and vain is the

7:140.t: He said: "Shall I seek for you a god other than the
God, when it is God Who hath endowed you with gifts above the nations

7:141.t: And remember We rescued you from Pharaoh's people, who afflicted you with the worst of penalties, who slew your male children and saved alive your females: in that was a momentous trial from your Lord

7:142.t: We appointed for Moses thirty nights, and completed
with his Lord, forty nights. And Moses had charged his brother Aaron
: "Act for me amongst my peopl e: Do right, and follow not the way of those who do mischief

7:143.t: When Moses came to the place appointed by Us, and his Lord addressed him, He said: "O my Lord! show
to me, that I may look upon thee." God said: "By no means canst thou see Me

; But look upon the mount; if it abide in its pla ce, then shalt thou see Me." When his Lord manifested His glory on the Mount, He made it as dust. And Moses fell down in a swoon. When he recovered his senses he said: "Glory be to Thee! to Thee I turn in repentance, and I am the first to believe

7:144.t: said: "O Moses! I have chosen thee above
which I give thee, and be of those who give thanks

7:145.t: And We ordained laws for him in the tablets in all matters, both commanding and explaining all things,
: "Take and hold these with firmness, and enjoin thy people to hold fast by the best in the precepts: soon shall I show you the ho mes of the wicked,-

7:146.t: Those who behave arrogantly on the earth in defiance of right - them will I turn away from My signs: Even if they see all the signs, they will not believe in them; and if they see the way of right conduct, they will not adopt it as the way; but if they see the way of error, that is the way they will adopt. For they have rejected our signs, and failed to take warning from them

7:147.t: Those who reject Our signs and the meeting in the Hereafter,- vain are their deeds: Can they expect to be rewarded except as they have wrought

7:148.t: The people of Moses made, in his absence, out of their ornaments, the image of calf,
: it seemed to low: did they not see that it could neither speak to them, nor show them the way? They took it for worship and they did wrong

7:149.t: When they repented, and saw that they had erred, they said: "If our Lord have not mercy upon us and forgive us, we shall indeed be of those who perish

7:150.t: When Moses came back to his people, angry and grieved, he said: "Evil it is that ye have done in my place in my absence: did ye make haste to bring on the judgment of your Lord?" He put down the tablets, seized his brother by

his head, and dragged him to him. Aaron said: "Son of my mother! the people did indeed reckon me as naught, and went near to slaying me! Make not the enemies rejoice over my misfortune, nor count thou me amongst the people of sin

7:151.t: Moses prayed: "O my Lord! forgive me and my brother! admit us to Thy mercy! for Thou art the Most Merciful of those who show mercy

7:152.t: will indeed be overwhelmed with wrath from their Lord, and with shame in this life: thus do We recompense those who invent

7:153.t: But those who do wrong but repent thereafter and
believe,- verily thy Lord is thereafter Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful

7:154.t: When the anger of Moses was appeased, he took up the tablets: in the writing thereon was guidance and Mercy for such as fear their Lord

7:155.t: And Moses chose seventy of his people for Our place of meeting: when they were seized with violent quaking, he prayed: "O my Lord! if it had been Thy will Thou couldst have destroyed, long before, both them and me: wouldst Thou destroy us for the deeds of the foolish ones among us? this is no more than Thy trial: by it Thou causest whom Thou wilt to stray, and Thou leadest whom Thou wilt into the right path. Thou art our Protector: so forgive us and give us Thy mercy; for Thou art the best of those who forgive

7:156.t: And ordain for us that which is good, in this life and in the Hereafter: for we have turned unto Thee." He said: "With My punishment I visit whom I will; but My mercy extendeth to all things. That
I shall ordain for those who do right, and practise regular charity, and those who believe in Our signs

7:157.t: Those who follow the apostle, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find mentioned in their own
,- in the law and the Gospel;- for he commands them what is just and forbids them what is evil; he allows them as lawful what is good
and prohibits them from what is bad

; He releases them from their heavy burdens and from the yokes that are upon them. So it is those who believe in him, honour him, help him, and follow the light which is sent down with him,- it is they who will prosper

7:158.t: day: "O men! I am sent unto you all, as the Apostle of God, to Whom belongeth the dominion of the heavens and the earth: there is no god but He: it is He That giveth both life and death. So believe in God and His Apostle, the Unlettered Prophe t, who believeth in God and His words: follow him that

7:159.t: Of the people of Moses there is a section who guide and do justice in the light of truth

7:160.t: We divided them into twelve tribes or nations. We directed Moses by inspiration, when his

people asked him for water: "Strike the rock with thy staff": out of it there gushed forth twelve springs: Each group knew its own place for w ater. We gave them the shade of clouds, and sent down to them manna and quails,
: "Eat of the good things We have provided for you":
; to Us they did no harm, but they harmed their own souls

7:161.t: And remember it was said to them: "Dwell in this town and eat therein as ye wish, but say the word of humility and enter the gate in a posture of humility: We shall forgive you your faults; We shall increase

7:162.t: But the transgressors among them changed the word from that which had been given them so we sent on them a plague from heaven. For that they repeatedly transgressed

7:163.t: Ask them concerning the town standing close by the sea. Behold! they transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath. For on the day of their Sabbath their fish did come to them, openly holding up their heads, but on the day they had no Sabbath, th ey came not: thus did We make a trial of them, for they were given to transgression

7:164.t: When some of them said: "Why do ye preach to a people whom God will destroy or visit with a terrible punishment?"- said the preachers:" To discharge our duty to your Lord, and perchance they may fear Him

7:165.t: When they disregarded the warnings that had been given them, We rescued those who forbade Evil; but We visited the wrong-doers with a grievous punishment because they were given to transgression

7:166.t: When in their insolence they transgressed
prohibitions, We said to them: "Be ye apes, despised and rejected

7:167.t: Behold! thy Lord did declare that He would send against them, to the Day of Judgment, those who would afflict them with grievous penalty. Thy Lord is quick in retribution, but He is also Oft-forgiving, Most Merciful

7:168.t: We broke them up into sections on this earth. There are among them some that are the righteous, and some that are the opposite. We have tried them with both prosperity and adversity: In order that they might turn

7:169.t: generation: They inherited the Book, but they chose
the vanities of this world, saying
, if similar vanities came their way, they would

seize them. Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not ascribe to God anything but the truth? and they study what is in the Book. But best for the righteous is the home in the Hereafter. Will ye not understand

7:170.t: As to those who hold fast by the Book and establish regular prayer,- never shall We suffer the reward of the righteous to perish

7:171.t: When We shook the Mount over them, as if it had been a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them
: "Hold firmly to what We have given you, and bring
to remembrance what is therein; perchance ye may fear God

7:172.t: When thy Lord drew forth from the Children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves,
, lest ye should say on the Day of Judgment: "Of this we were never mindful

7:173.t: Or lest ye should say: "Our fathers before us may have taken false gods, but we are
descendants after them: wilt Thou then destroy us because of the deeds of men who were futile

7:174.t: Thus do We explain the signs in detail; and perchance they may turn

7:175.t: Relate to them the story of the man to whom We sent Our signs, but he passed them by: so Satan followed him up, and he went astray

7:176.t: If it had been Our will, We should have elevated him with Our signs; but he inclined to the earth, and followed his own vain desires. His similitude is that of a dog: if you attack him, he lolls out his tongue, or if you leave him alone, he
lolls out his tongue. That is the similitude of those who reject Our signs; So relate the story; perchance they may reflect

7:177.t: Evil as an example are people who reject Our signs and wrong their own souls

7:178.t: Whom God doth guide,- he is on the right path: whom He rejects from His guidance,- such are the persons who perish

7:179.t: Many are the Jinns and men we have made for Hell: They have hearts wherewith they understand not, eyes wherewith they see not, and ears wherewith they hear not. They are like cattle,- nay more misguided: for they are heedless

7:180.t: The most beautiful names belong to God: so call on him by them; but shun such men as use profanity in his names: for what they do, they will soon be requited

7:181.t: Of those We have created are people who direct
with truth. And dispense justice therewith

7:182.t: Those who reject Our signs, We shall gradually visit with punishment, in ways they perceive not

7:183.t: Respite will I grant unto them: for My scheme is strong

7:184.t: Do they not reflect? Their companion is not seized with madness: he is but a perspicuous warner

7:185.t: Do they see nothing in the government of the heavens and the earth and all that God hath created?
that it may well be that their terms is nigh drawing to an end? In what message after this will they then believe

7:186.t: To such as God rejects from His guidance, there can be no guide: He will leave them in their trespasses, wandering in distraction

7:187.t: Hour - when will be its appointed time? Say: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord

: None but He can reveal as to when it will occur. Heavy were its burden through the heavens and the earth. Only, all of a sudden will it come to you." They ask thee as if thou Wert eager in search thereof: Say: "The knowledge thereof is with God

7:188.t: Say: "I have no power over any good or harm to myself except as God willeth. If I had knowledge of the unseen, I should have multiplied all good, and no evil should have touched me: I am but a warner, and a bringer of glad tidings to those who have faith

7:189.t: It is He Who created you from a single person, and made his mate of like nature, in order that he might dwell with her
. When they are united, she bears a light burden and carries it about
. When she grows heavy, they both pray to God their Lord,
: "If Thou givest us a goodly child, we vow we shall

7:190.t: But when He giveth them a goodly child, they ascribe to others a share in the gift they have received: but God is exalted high above the partners they ascribe to Him

7:191.t: Do they indeed ascribe to Him as partners things that can create nothing, but are themselves created

7:192.t: No aid can they give them, nor can they aid themselves

7:193.t: If ye call them to guidance, they will not obey: For you it is the same whether ye call them or ye hold your peace

7:194.t: Verily those whom ye call upon besides God are servants like unto you: Call upon them, and let them listen to your prayer, if ye are

7:195.t: Have they feet to walk with? Or hands to lay hold with? Or eyes to see with? Or ears to hear with? Say: "Call your 'god-partners', scheme
against me, and give me no respite

7:196.t: For my Protector is God, Who revealed the Book
, and He will choose and befriend the righteous

7:197.t: But those ye call upon besides Him, are unable to help you, and indeed to help themselves

7:198.t: If thou callest them to guidance, they hear not. Thou wilt see them looking at thee, but they see not

7:199.t: Hold to forgiveness; command what is right; But turn away from the ignorant

7:200.t: If a suggestion from Satan assail thy
, seek refuge with God; for He heareth and knoweth

7:201.t: Those who fear God, when a thought of evil from Satan assaults them, bring God to remembrance, when lo! they see

7:202.t: plunge them deeper into error, and never relax

7:203.t: If thou bring them not a revelation, they say: "Why hast thou not got it together?" Say: "I but follow what is revealed to me from my Lord: this is
lights from your Lord, and Guidance, and mercy, for any who have faith

7:204.t: When the Qur'an is read, listen to it with attention, and hold your peace: that ye may receive Mercy

7:205.t: Bring thy Lord to remembrance in thy
soul, with humility and in reverence, without loudness in words, in the mornings and evenings; and be not thou of those who are unheedful

7:206.t: Those who are near to thy Lord, disdain not to do Him worship: They celebrate His praises, and bow down before Him

8:1.t: spoils are at the disposal of God and the Apostle: So fear God, and keep straight the relations between yourselves: Obey God and His Apostle, if ye do believe

8:2.t: For, Believers are those who, when God is mentioned, feel a tremor in their hearts, and when they hear His signs rehearsed, find their faith strengthened, and put

8:3.t: Who establish regular prayers and spend
out of the gifts We have given them for sustenance

8:4.t: Such in truth are the believers: they have grades of dignity with their Lord, and forgiveness, and generous sustenance

8:5.t: Just as thy Lord ordered thee out of thy house in truth, even though a party among the Believers disliked it

8:6.t: Disputing with thee concerning the truth after it was made manifest, as if they were being driven to death and they

8:7.t: Behold! God promised you one of the two
parties, that it should be yours: Ye wished that the one unarmed should be yours, but God willed to justify the Truth according to His words and to cut off the roots of the Unbelievers

8:8.t: That He might justify Truth and prove Falsehood false, distasteful though it be to those in guilt

8:9.t: Remember ye implored the assistance of your Lord, and He answered you: "I will assist you with a thousand of the angels, ranks on ranks

8:10.t: God made it but a message of hope, and an assurance to your hearts:
there is no help except from God: and God is Exalted in Power, Wise

8:11.t: Remember He covered you with a sort of drowsiness, to give you calm as from Himself, and he caused rain to descend on you from heaven, to clean you therewith, to remove from you the stain of Satan, to strengthen your hearts, and to plant your feet firmly therewith

8:12.t: Remember thy Lord inspired the angels
: "I am with you: give firmness to the Believers: I will instil terror into the hearts of the Unbelievers: smite ye above their necks and smite all their finger-tips off them

8:13.t: This because they contended against God and His Apostle: If any contend against God and His Apostle, God is strict in punishment

8:14.t: : for those who resist God, is the penalty of the Fire

8:15.t: O ye who believe! when ye meet the Unbelievers in hostile array, never turn your backs to them

8:16.t: If any do turn his back to them on such a day - unless it be in a stratagem of war, or to retreat to a troop
- he draws on himself the wrath of God, and his abode is Hell,- an evil refuge

8:17.t: It is not ye who slew them; it was God: when thou threwest
, it was not thy act, but God's: in order that He might test the Believers by a gracious trial from Himself: for God is He Who heareth and knoweth

8:18.t: That, and also because God is He Who makes feeble the plans and stratagem of the Unbelievers

8:19.t: if ye prayed for victory and judgment, now hath the judgment come to you: if ye desist
, it will be best for you: if ye return
, so shall We. Not the least good will your forces be to you even if they were multiplied: for verily God is with those who believe

8:20.t: O ye who believe! Obey God and His Apostle, and turn not away from him when ye hear

8:21.t: Nor be like those who say, "We hear," but listen not

8:22.t: For the worst of beasts in the sight of God are the deaf and the dumb,- those who understand not

8:23.t: If God had found in them any good. He would indeed have made them listen:
, if He had made them listen, they would but have turned back and declined

8:24.t: O ye who believe! give your response to God and His Apostle, when He calleth you to that which will give you life; and know that God cometh in between a man and his heart, and that it is He to Whom ye shall

8:25.t: And fear tumult or oppression, which affecteth not in particular
those of you who do wrong: and know that God is strict in punishment

8:26.t: Call to mind when ye were a small

, despised through the land, and afraid that men might despoil and kidnap you; But He provided a safe asylum for you, strengthened you with His aid, and gave you Good things for sustenance: that ye migh t be grateful

8:27.t: O ye that believe! betray not the trust of God and the Apostle, nor misappropriate knowingly things entrusted to you

8:28.t: And know ye that your possessions and your progeny are but a trial; and that it is God with Whom lies your highest reward

8:29.t: O ye who believe! if ye fear God, He will grant you a criterion
to judge between right and wrong
you, and forgive you: for God is the Lord of grace unbounded

. They plot and plan, and God too plans; but the best of planners is God

8:31.t: When Our Signs are rehearsed to them, they say: "We have heard this
: if we wished, we could say
like these: these are nothing but tales of the ancients

8:34.t: But what plea have they that God should not punish them, when they keep out

, "Taste ye the penalty because ye blasphemed

from the path of God, and so will they continue to spend; but in the end they will have
regrets and sighs; at length they will be overcome: and the Unbelievers will be gathered together to Hell

a matter of warning for them

8:39.t: And fight them on until there is no more tumult or oppression, and there prevail justice and faith in God altogether and everywhere; but if they cease, verily God doth see all that they do

8:40.t: If they refuse, be sure that God is your Protector - the best to protect and the best to help

, a fifth share is assigned to God,- and to the Apostle, and to near relatives, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer,- if ye do believe in God and in the revelation We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Testing,- the Day of the meeting of the two forces. For God hath power over all things

8:42.t: Remember ye were on the hither side of the valley, and they on the farther side, and the caravan on lower ground than ye. Even if ye had made a mutual appointment to meet, ye would certainly have failed in the appointment: But
, t hat God might accomplish a matter already enacted; that those who died might die after a clear Sign
, and those who lived might live after a Clear Sign
. And verily God is He Who heareth and knoweth

8:45.t: O ye who believe! When ye meet a force, be firm, and call God in remembrance much

8:46.t: And obey God and His Apostle; and fall into no disputes, lest ye lose heart and your power depart; and be patient and persevering: For God is with those who patiently persevere

souls: and verily God is He Who heareth and knoweth

8:59.t: Let not the unbelievers think that they can get the better

the enemies, of God and your enemies, and others besides, whom ye may not know, but whom God doth know. Whatever ye shall spend in the cause of God, shall be repaid unto you, and ye shall not be treated unjustly

and unto those who follow thee among the Believers

8:65.t: O Apostle! rouse the Believers to the fight. If there are twenty amongst you, patient and persevering, they will vanquish two hundred: if a hundred, they will vanquish a thousand of the Unbelievers: for these are a people without understanding

, for He knoweth that there is a weak spot in you: But

, they have already been in treason against God, and so hath He given

God seeth all that ye do

8:73.t: The Unbelievers are protectors, one of another: Unless ye do this,
, there would be tumult and oppression on earth, and great mischief

9:1.t: of immunity from God and His Apostle, to those of the Pagans with whom ye have contracted mutual alliances

9:2.t: Go ye, then, for four months, backwards and forwards,
, throughout the land, but know ye that ye cannot frustrate God
but that God will cover with shame those who reject Him

9:3.t: And an announcement from God and His Apostle, to the people
on the day of the Great Pilgrimage,- that God and His Apostle dissolve
obligations with the Pagans. If then, ye repent, it were best for you; but if ye turn away, know ye that ye cannot frustrate God. And proclaim a grievous penalty to those who reject Faith

9:4.t: not dissolved with those Pagans with whom ye have entered into alliance and who have not subsequently failed you in aught, nor aided any one against you. So fulfil your engagements with them to the end of their term: for God loveth the righteous

9:5.t: But when the forbidden months are past, then fight and slay the Pagans wherever ye find them, an seize them, beleaguer them, and lie in wait for them in every stratagem
; but if they repent, and establish regular prayers and practise r egular charity, then open the way for them: for God is Oft-forgiving, Most Merciful

9:6.t: If one amongst the Pagans ask thee for asylum, grant it to him, so that he may hear the word of God; and then escort him to where he can be secure. That is because they are men without knowledge

9:7.t: How can there be a league, before God and His Apostle, with the Pagans, except those with whom ye made a treaty near the sacred Mosque? As long as these stand true to you, stand ye true to them: for God doth love the righteous

9:8.t: can there be such a league
, seeing that if they get an advantage over you, they respect not in you the ties either of kinship or of covenant? With
their mouths they entice you, but their hearts are averse from you; and m ost of them are rebellious and wicked

9:9.t: The Signs of God have they sold for a miserable price, and
have they hindered from His way: evil indeed are the deeds they have done

9:10.t: In a Believer they respect not the ties either of kinship or of covenant! It is they who have transgressed all bounds

9:11.t: , if they repent, establish regular prayers, and practise regular charity,- they are your brethren in Faith:
do We explain the Signs in detail, for those who understand

9:12.t: But if they violate their oaths after their covenant, and taunt you for your Faith,- fight ye the chiefs of Unfaith: for their oaths are nothing to them: that thus they may be restrained

you? Do ye fear them? Nay, it is God Whom ye should more justly fear, if ye believe

9:14.t: Fight them, and God will punish them by your hands, cover them with shame, help you
over them, heal the breasts of Believers

9:15.t: And still the indignation of their hearts. For God will turn
to whom He will; and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise

9:16.t: Or think ye that ye shall be abandoned, as though God did not know those among you who strive with might and main, and take none for friends and protectors except God, His Apostle, and the
Believers? But God is well- acquainted w ith

9:18.t: The mosques of God shall be visited and maintained by such as believe in God and the Last Day, establish regular prayers, and practise regular charity, and fear none
except God. It is they who are expected to be on true guidance

9:19.t: Do ye make the giving of drink to pilgrims, or the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque, equal to
those who believe in God and the Last Day, and strive with might and main in the cause of God? They are not comparable in the sight of God: and God guides not those who do wrong

9:20.t: Those who believe, and suffer exile and strive with might and main, in God's cause, with their goods and their persons, have the highest rank in the sight of God: they are the people who will achieve

9:21.t: Their Lord doth give them glad tidings of a Mercy from Himself, of His good pleasure, and of gardens for them, wherein are delights that endure

9:22.t: They will dwell therein for ever. Verily in God's presence is a reward, the greatest

9:23.t: O ye who believe! take not for protectors your fathers and your brothers if they love infidelity above Faith: if any of you do so, they do wrong

9:24.t: Say: If it be that your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your mates, or your kindred; the wealth that ye have gained; the commerce in which ye fear a decline: or the dwellings in which ye delight - are dearer to you than God, or His Apostle, or the striving in His cause;- then wait until God brings about His decision: and God guides not the rebellious

9:25.t: Assuredly God did help you in many battle-fields and on the day of Hunain: Behold! your great numbers elated you, but they availed you naught: the land, for all that it is wide, did constrain you, and ye turned back in retreat

9:26.t: But God did pour His calm on the Apostle and on the Believers, and sent down forces which ye saw not: He punished the Unbelievers; thus doth He reward those without Faith

9:27.t: Again will God, after this, turn
to whom He will: for God is Oft- forgiving, Most Merciful

9:28.t: O ye who believe! Truly the Pagans are unclean; so let them not, after this year of theirs, approach the Sacred Mosque. And if ye fear poverty, soon will God enrich you, if He wills, out of His bounty, for God is All-knowing, All-wise

But the word of God is exalted to the heights: for God is Exalted in might, Wise
